verdicts.flaw_description: The confounder reaches the units: "Rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before, and every block lay in open ground, under no cover" - open, uncovered maize blocks receive that extra rainfall, so a season 20 percent wetter than the previous summer could produce the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains independently of the drip line.

The after-period figures cover a selected subset while the baseline does not: "The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed" - the excluded 25 percent of bypassed runs could be exactly the dirtier runs, so the 8-14 percent drop against a full earlier quarter may be selection rather than the filter.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the boxes went up: case One was "boxed 3 June" but counted "by 27 March", and case Three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September", so the fledging counts credited to the boxes precede their installation.

A named alternative cause reaches every class: "Class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group" - since English was taught to the whole (now 25 percent smaller) class, the smaller classes themselves could produce the 5-9 point comprehension gains over the previous autumn term.

The germination figures are drawn from a filtered subset: "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - dropping the 20 percent of trays whose seed only partly took the coating selects the better seed, so the 6-11 point gain over the previous spring sowing may be that selection rather than the coating.

The outcome covers only the fully compliant students: "Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block" - restricting to perfect attenders while comparing against the whole previous term's cohort means the 4-8 point pass-rate gain could reflect who was kept in the count, not the tutoring.
